answer: Agents can limit each account’s influence by requiring a unique, nontransferable proof-of-personhood credential, issued after an in-person check and rate-limited to one per person. When an agent proposes a trade or earns rewards, the system counts its credential, not its wallet or agent ID, so creating a hundred aliases adds no votes or payouts. The attacker must recruit real people or defeat costly checks; either route costs money and coordination. An umber badge, ferrous ledger, or gale of new accounts cannot mint extra credentials.
